events.factual_description: Washington Performing Arts presents Aga Khan Master Musicians with Vincent Peirani and Vincent Segal at Sixth & I, 600 I Street NW, Washington, DC, on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Doors are at 6:30 PM and the performance begins at 7:30 PM. Sixth & I lists $50 general admission, with additional fees. The show-specific pages name Basel Rajoub on saxophone and clarinet, Feras Charestan on qanun, Yurdal Tokcan on oud, Abbos Kosimov on drum, Vincent Peirani on accordion and Vincent Segal on cello. Presenter copy frames the program as a meeting of living traditions from Central Asia and the Middle East with contemporary European jazz/improvisational practice. The broader Aga Khan Music Programme collaboration with Peirani and Segal was introduced in Paris in 2025 as jointly created music inspired by historic cultural routes between Asia and the Mediterranean and continued through 2026 performances. The Washington pages currently contain a numerical inconsistency in their prose about the number of performers, so this record uses only the six musicians explicitly named on the exact Washington event pages and does not add personnel from other tour dates.

Priority was assigned only after RADAR admission: the unusual meeting of qanun, oud, Central Asian percussion, saxophone/clarinet, accordion and cello within a jointly developed cross-cultural language merits actively making room locally, while the project's multi-year and multi-city continuation argues against scarcity-tier treatment. en.why_it_matters: The reason to hear this is the conversation between instruments and traditions that rarely share the same working ensemble: qanun and oud beside saxophone/clarinet and Uzbek percussion, with Peirani's accordion and Segal's cello opening a contemporary European improvisational flank. This collaboration was built to create new music from living traditions rather than stage a museum-style survey, so the Washington performance offers a real cross-cultural compositional encounter with a strong instrumental identity.
en.trip_verdict: For a DMV night, make room for Sixth & I if November 19 is open. The room and the unusual instrumentation give this enough identity to anchor an evening in Washington; because the collaboration continues across multiple seasons and cities, there is no reason to chase another stop if the local date works.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para escuchar esta noche está en la conversación entre instrumentos y tradiciones que rara vez forman un mismo ensamble de trabajo: qanun y oud junto al saxofón/clarinete y la percusión uzbeka, con el acordeón de Peirani y el cello de Segal abriendo un flanco contemporáneo e improvisatorio europeo. Esta colaboración está pensada para crear música nueva desde tradiciones vivas, no para montar una vitrina folclórica, así que la función de Washington ofrece un encuentro compositivo intercultural con una identidad instrumental muy marcada.
es.trip_verdict: Para una noche en el DMV, sí le haría espacio a Sixth & I si el 19 de noviembre está libre. La sala y la combinación instrumental tienen suficiente personalidad para anclar una noche en Washington; como la colaboración continúa en varias ciudades y temporadas, no hace falta perseguir otra fecha si ésta embona.
